_about: What the engine can draw, scored by how much work and risk each tag adds to a scene. cost 0-10 (0 = free, 10 = new art + several rounds). status: proven (a finished short used it), risky (worked after several fix rounds), missing (never built). untested (the template claims it or we plan it, but we never rendered it). Evidence is from the bridge template and the rail test short. Re-fit after every finished short.

place.street.note: town street / square, the template's home ground
place.street.evidence: template claim only, never rendered by us (corrected 2026-11-12)

place.bridge_river.evidence: template claim only, never rendered by us (corrected 2026-11-12)

place.office.note: one room, desk, wall props; camera must keep the desk from covering the frame

place.canyon.note: mesas read as skyscrapers unless silhouettes are varied; needs fog depth
place.canyon.instead: use one street, square or bridge; keep far hills as a flat backdrop

place.interior_other.note: any room that is not the office: new walls, props, lighting
place.interior_other.instead: use the office room we have, or keep the scene outdoors

place.sea_ship.instead: move the story to a harbour wall or bridge, tell the sea part in narration

place.space.instead: cannot be drawn; change the setting

chars.1_3.note: 1-3 cards with ink outlines, expressions, hip/point/cross/temple/reach poses

chars.crowd.evidence: template claim only, never rendered by us (corrected 2026-11-12)

chars.4_8_named.note: each needs its own outfit, silhouette and staging
chars.4_8_named.instead: cut to 3 named characters, show the rest as a crowd
chars.4_8_named.evidence: never rendered by us; the rail short had 3 characters, 2 on screen

chars.animal.instead: replace the animal with a person or an object

prop.kit_static.note: Kenney CC0 kit pieces, lamps, fences, crates

prop.text_sign.note: newspaper/sign/chart with readable words: size, angle and crop problems
prop.text_sign.instead: use one big upright sign or newspaper facing the camera, 3 to 5 words

prop.vehicle_moving.note: own-built trains; timing, framing and scale all needed rounds
prop.vehicle_moving.instead: show the vehicle parked or entering once; tell the rest in narration

prop.readable_detail.note: a small detail the viewer must see (a gap, a crack, a coin): needs close camera + exaggerated geometry
prop.readable_detail.instead: make it large, one close insert shot, one idea per shot

action.walk.evidence: template claim only, never rendered by us (corrected 2026-11-12)

action.object_fall.note: coin/paper dropping on the beat; physics arc must be authored
action.object_fall.instead: use one object, one drop, one close insert

action.tool_use.note: sawing, hammering, throwing: no animation exists
action.tool_use.instead: show the result, not the action (the cut rail, not the sawing)

action.fight_chase.instead: cannot be drawn; show before and after

fx.explosion_fire.instead: cannot be drawn; show the aftermath

fx.weather.instead: cannot be drawn; use a clear day

light.golden.note: pink/purple tint came back every round; shadows violet, lit areas warm
light.golden.instead: keep golden hour to the last 1-2 scenes only

light.night.note: no night grade or lamps tuned
light.night.instead: use day or indoor light; say 'night' in narration

camera.orbit.note: keep subject in frame through the move
camera.orbit.instead: use a push-in or a glide

camera.insert_detail.note: cut to a close insert of a small object
camera.insert_detail.instead: max 2 inserts per short, each 30-40 frames

state.geometry_change.note: scene geometry that changes over time and must read (gap closes, rail buckles)
state.geometry_change.instead: change the story so nothing in the scene changes shape; show before and after as two scenes

place.town_buildings.note: houses, shops, a street of buildings (the rail short had canyon, bridges and one office only)
place.town_buildings.instead: keep to one open square with 2-3 simple props, tell the town in narration

place.market.instead: one stall and one table, not a full market

place.palace.note: grand hall, throne, large decorated interior
place.palace.instead: use the office room dressed as a hall, or move outdoors

action.mouth_sync.note: mouth moving with speech; the rail short has no mouth sync
action.mouth_sync.instead: keep the mouth still or closed; captions and voice carry the line

limits._note: max_seconds is the plan limit. proven_max_seconds is the longest short the engine has actually rendered (56.7 s).

_source_kinds.existing_asset: CC0 kit pieces already in the repo (Kenney)
_source_kinds.procedural: built in code by the engine (cards, props, sky, trains, grade)
_source_kinds.animation_supported: a movement/camera move the engine already performs
_source_kinds.new_work: needs new assets, new animation logic or a different approach: not available

starter.note: the profile we aim for. Scenes stay 8-10 on purpose: simple scripts need few scenes. Real results so far: rail (19 scenes, difficulty 100) took 7 rounds and ended at 34/70; Bell (9 scenes / 11 shots, scorer guess difficulty 81 and 9 rounds) was stopped by the score rule after 4 rounds, 37 -> 40 -> 44 -> 41 /70 (best 44, not ready). The scorer over-guessed the rounds for Bell, but its 34-39/70 guess was too low for the best round; 4 rounds is one sample, so not sure it is a good fit. Rail was an exception, not the target. Words are per the measured 3.7 words per second (one sample).

explainer.note: not yet produced; use at your own risk, expect extra rounds

comedy.note: not yet produced; timing (beats before words) will need testing

words_per_second.basis: measured once: the rail short has 212 words in 56.7 s. One short only, re-measure after every finished short.
